sn12.16:1.1: [While the Exalted One was staying] at Sāvatthi,
sn12.16:1.2: a certain monk came into his presence, and when he had saluted him he sat down at one side and said:—
sn12.16:1.3: Lord, we hear the word Dhamma-teacher, Dhamma-teacher.
sn12.16:2.1: If one of you, monk, teaches a doctrine of revulsion from decay-and-death, of its fading away, of the ceasing thereof, this is enough for him to be called Dhamma-teaching Brother.
sn12.16:2.2: If a monk have practised himself in this revulsion, [making it] fade away and cease, this is enough for him to be called one versed in that which is in conformity with the Dhamma.
sn12.16:2.3: If a monk from revulsion, from [making it] fade away and cease, be set free from any form of grasping, this is enough for him to be called 'one who hath won Nibbana in this life.'
sn12.16:3.1: In the same way you can so call a monk after this threefold manner if he teach, if he practise, if he be in consequence set free from any form of grasping with respect to birth …
sn12.16:3.11: If one of you, monk, teaches a doctrine of revulsion from ignorance, of its fading away, of the ceasing thereof, this is enough for him to be called Dhamma-teaching Brother.
sn12.16:3.12: If a monk have practised himself in this revulsion from ignorance, [making it] fade away and cease, this is enough for him to be called one versed in that which is in conformity with the Dhamma.
sn12.16:3.13: If a monk from revulsion from ignorance, from [making it] fade away and cease, be set free from any form of grasping, this is enough for him to be called 'one who hath won Nibbana in this life.'
